description.text: The Kāpiti Coast runs from Paekākāriki in the south to Ōtaki, the northernmost point of the Wellington Region, between the Tasman Sea and the mountains. Its beach towns lie 40–70 km north of Wellington and face Kāpiti Island, a 19.65 km² predator-free island that gave the district its name. Paraparaumu is the biggest town and commercial centre, and the Kapiti Line train from Wellington takes 54 minutes to reach it. Queen Elizabeth Park holds the last area of natural dunes on the coast.

Six settlements, from Paekākāriki to Ōtaki, make up the Kāpiti Coast, with unspoilt beaches, rivers and villages between the mountains and the sea. Kāpiti Island sits 5 km offshore, a 10 km-long reserve that only authorised operators can land on. Ōtaki, at the north end, has Māori cultural heritage and the Rangiātea church, rebuilt in 2003, while Coast35, a sealed shared trail, links Paekākāriki and Ōtaki. Wellington is 40–70 km south, most of it on State Highway 1 and the Kapiti Line.

The Kāpiti Coast is a chain of beach towns along State Highway 1 and the Kapiti Line, from Paekākāriki to Ōtaki. Offshore, Kāpiti Island is about 10 km long and about 2 km wide, and the district takes its name from it. On land, the options range from the 10 km Escarpment Track above the sea to Southward Car Museum, with more than 400 vehicles, and Ngā Manu's bird reserve. Beaches here range from remote driftwood stretches at Te Horo to family beaches at Paraparaumu and Raumati.

tips.title: Book the island early
tips.detail: You can only land on Kāpiti Island with an authorised operator, from the Kapiti Boating Club at Paraparaumu Beach. Summer bookings need to be made well in advance, and bags are checked for pests before boarding.

tips.title: Confirm the weather
tips.detail: Island trips depend on conditions, so confirm with the operator on the morning. The operator's homepage showed a cancelled ferry on the day of research.

tips.title: Walk the track one way
tips.detail: The Escarpment Track has about 1,200 steps and no facilities, and is not recommended for anyone with vertigo or low fitness. Walk it one way and take the train back, as there are stations at both ends.

tips.title: No private landings
tips.detail: Private boats cannot land on Kāpiti Island. The operator's day-trip price includes the DOC permit, and bags are inspected for pests before you board.

tips.title: Trains end at Waikanae
tips.detail: The Kapiti Line from Wellington reaches Paraparaumu in 54 minutes and terminates at Waikanae. Ōtaki and Ngā Manu need a car or bus, and local buses link Paraparaumu, the beaches and Waikanae.

tips.title: Park gates close early
tips.detail: Queen Elizabeth Park is open to walkers at all times, but vehicle gates close at 6pm from April to September and 9pm from October to March.

tips.title: Check nesting closures
tips.detail: The island's Boulder Bank Loop is closed October to March for nesting seabirds, which overlaps the best beach months.

tips.title: Expect a steep climb
tips.detail: The Escarpment Track rises to about 220 m over two swing bridges and is rated intermediate. It crosses privately owned farmland, so stay on the track.

tips.title: Trams run on weekends
tips.detail: The Wellington Tramway Museum in Queen Elizabeth Park runs trams at weekends only, per a 2016 Wikivoyage listing (11am–4:30pm). Check before you go.
tips.caveat: Wikivoyage 2016 listing; research.json says council says the same but the museum site was not loaded. Keep only if the owner accepts the caveat.

spots.name: Kāpiti Island
spots.bio: A predator-free island reserve off Paraparaumu Beach, reached only by licensed boat, where kākā, hihi and kiwi live wild and a track climbs to the 521 m summit.
spots.hours: Daytime tours only; operator day trips depart from 8:00 AM, weather permitting
spots.hours_note: Operator: about 5.5 hours on the island (Rangatira) or 4.5 hours (Waiorua/north end)
spots.cost_note: Operator 'from' adult prices: Waiorua half-day $139, Rangatira day trip $169; includes return ferry, DOC permit and intro talk.
spots.coordinates_note: island centroid, unverified landing points; run audit-spot-coordinates (a centroid in water is correct for an island)

spots.name: Paekākāriki
spots.bio: A beachfront village of about 1,700 people at the south end of the coast, with a surf beach, a railway station museum and the foot of the Escarpment Track.

spots.name: Raumati Beach
spots.bio: A beachside village facing Kāpiti Island, good for surfcasting and swimming, with Marine Gardens holding a miniature railway and a paddling pool and playground.
spots.caveat: 'facing Kāpiti Island' comes from research.json spot suggestion; Wikivoyage supports the surfcasting/swimming and Marine Gardens facts

spots.name: Southward Car Museum
spots.bio: A purpose-built hall of more than 400 vehicles and exhibits assembled by Sir Len Southward, with a 474-seat theatre housing a 1929 Wurlitzer organ.
spots.hours: 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM daily (last entry 4:00 PM); closed Good Friday and Christmas Day

spots.name: Paraparaumu Beach
spots.bio: A sandy beach opposite Kāpiti Island, sheltered by it and safe for children, with a playground and skate park, and the departure point for island boats.
spots.coordinates_note: Wikivoyage beach point is -40.8861,174.9815 (about 900 m north); audit before shipping

spots.name: Paekākāriki Escarpment Track
spots.bio: A 10 km section of Te Araroa between Paekākāriki and Pukerua Bay, climbing to about 220 m with about 1,200 steps, two swing bridges and views over the coast to Kāpiti Island.
spots.ticketUrl_note: No steward page verified (research.json); omit and say so in summary
spots.coordinates_note: Paekākāriki station end, per caller correction; trailhead unverified, run audit-spot-coordinates

spots.name: Ōtaki Beach
spots.bio: A surf and fishing beach at the north end of the coast, 4 km from Ōtaki town, with the Tararua Ranges behind and a cairn marking two 1878 shipwrecks.
spots.note: No promenade and no island-view claim, per caller correction and research.json

spots.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
spots.bio: A regional park between Paekākāriki and Raumati South with the coast's last natural dunes, restored wetlands, the only kahikatea forest remnant on the coast and the Wellington Tramway Museum.
spots.hours: Open to foot traffic always; vehicle gates 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM (1 Apr–30 Sep) and 6:00 AM – 9:00 PM (1 Oct–31 Mar)
spots.caveat: Kapiti Coast Council page gives different gate hours (8 AM start); Greater Wellington, the manager, is used

spots.name: Ngā Manu Nature Reserve
spots.bio: A 14-hectare bird reserve in Waikanae with aviaries, a nocturnal house with kiwi and tuatara, eel feeding and a bush walk through a remnant of coastal swamp forest.

spots.name: Waikanae Beach
spots.bio: A 2.4 km beach at the Waikanae River mouth, beside an estuary scientific reserve with more than 60 bird species.
